summary: Source-anchored research for Atlas Query Targeting alerts. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: A high Query Targeting ratio is a triage signal, not proof of a problem: a MongoDB community forum respondent notes the warning by itself does not indicate a problem, but might if there is a performance impact, and asks for the pipeline, execution plan and indexes before advising. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/problem-query-targeting-scanned-objects-returned-above-1000/151062

Work beyond ordinary application reads can contribute to Query Targeting ratios. Atlas documents that MongoDB Search (mongot) change-stream cursors can raise the ratio; a Meteor issue thread also contains user reports associating Atlas alerts with oplog tailing, so include background consumers when correlating an alert with workload activity. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-conditions/ ; https://forums.meteor.com/t/galaxy-mongo-issue-any-theories-spiked-query-targeting-scanned-objects-returned-ratio/50115

MongoDB says Query Targeting alerts commonly occur when no index supports a query or an existing index only partially supports it. Change-stream cursors used by MongoDB Search `mongot` to maintain Search indexes can also contribute to the Query Targeting ratio. (high confidence)

Datadog's Atlas integration lists `mongodb.atlas.querystats.docs_examined_ratio` and `mongodb.atlas.querystats.keys_examined_ratio` per query shape; when enabled on a supported M10+ cluster, these metrics provide a query-shape view that can help investigate an aggregate Atlas alert. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

One Query Targeting alert does not identify one triggering query: Atlas computes a sampled server-wide metric, while the Query Profiler shows operations that meet Atlas's slow-query criteria. Atlas warns that automatic thresholds can leave operations contributing to the ratio out of the logs. Correlate the alert window with historical metrics and logs, then inspect representative operations with cursor.explain(). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Atlas warns that it might not log the individual operations that contribute to Query Targeting ratios, because of automatically set thresholds. A 2018-2019 MongoDB community Google Groups thread reports the same symptom: an empty Performance Advisor and no identifiable inefficient query in the downloaded logs. So an empty profiler or advisor view does not establish that no operation contributed to the alert. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting/ ; https://groups.google.com/g/mongodb-user/c/JNz0QuHM5EA

The Query Targeting alert is raised on the ratio of documents scanned to documents returned, not on elapsed time. Percona's MongoDB Instances Compare dashboard shows a Scan Ratios panel separately from an average operation Latency panel. A MongoDB community respondent notes the warning might matter if there is a performance impact, so check latency before treating a high ratio as a user-visible slowdown. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-conditions/ ; https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/2/details/dashboards/dashboard-mongodb-instances-compare.html ; https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/problem-query-targeting-scanned-objects-returned-above-1000/151062

Atlas defines two Query Targeting alert conditions: Scanned Objects / Returned compares documents scanned with documents returned, while Scanned / Returned compares index keys scanned with documents returned. Either condition might indicate a missing or inefficient index. (high confidence)

Atlas evaluates Scanned Objects / Returned using the ratio of average documents scanned to average documents returned across server operations during a sampling period; the documented default threshold is 1000:1. Scanned / Returned uses a user-defined threshold and is not enabled by default. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Query Shape Reports can narrow an investigation after a Scanned Objects / Returned alert: current Atlas documentation limits automatic eligibility to dedicated M10-or-higher clusters running MongoDB 8.0 or later, and reports list up to five query shapes with at least 10 executions in the three-day reporting period. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Atlas defines `Query Targeting: Scanned Objects / Returned` using documents scanned relative to documents returned, and `Query Targeting: Scanned / Returned` using index keys examined relative to documents returned. Atlas documentation reports a default 1000:1 threshold for the document-scan alert and says the index-key alert is not enabled by default. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-19)

Atlas evaluates the default scanned-objects condition from the average documents scanned relative to the average documents returned server-wide across all operations during a sampling period; this alert is not a per-query ratio threshold. (high confidence)
